turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning. I've done your observations before the doctor sees you. Blood pressure is one hundred and forty-eight over ninety-two, pulse seventy-eight, oxygen sat ninety-seven percent.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Is ninety-seven okay? I don't know, sister.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): That's perfectly fine. Doctor Pillay is ready, you and your wife can go through.
[SEG0004] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hello, come in, have a seat. I'm Doctor Pillay. How are you keeping?
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): Not bad, doctor. I'm just here for a check-up. The wife made the booking. I'm sixty-three this year.
[SEG0006] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He hasn't been near a doctor since we moved into the flat in Morningside. I had to nag him.
[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): Fair enough, we'll take our time. How have you been feeling in yourself?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Mostly okay. A bit tired some days. I don't know, doctor, I wouldn't have come on my own.
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any chest pain?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No chest pain at all.
[SEG0011] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): David. You stop halfway up the stairs and you hold your chest. Same when you walk fast to the robot.
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): It's not pain. It's more a tight feeling across the chest. Only when I climb the stairs or walk fast. If I take it slow, nothing.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): Shame, that sounds unpleasant. When did that tight feeling start?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. Maybe a few weeks. I can't say when, exactly.
[SEG0015] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Don't listen to the few weeks. It's been two months, easy. And it's every time he takes those stairs.
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Not every time. Only if I rush. And two months sounds too long. I really don't know.
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): And if you stop and rest, does it ease off?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja. I stand for about a minute and it goes, then I'm alright.
[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): Do you get short of breath at the same time?
[SEG0020] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yes he does. Huffing, and he can't finish a sentence on the way to the shops.
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I don't get short of breath. I talk fine. She's worrying over nothing, it's just the tightness.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'll note that you see it differently. Does it spread to the arm or the jaw?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): No, arm is fine, jaw is fine.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sweating, or feeling sick with it?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): No sweating. And I don't feel sick. Tummy's been okay.
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): How's your sleep, and passing urine?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Sleep's fine. Urine is normal, I think. Nothing strange.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): Are you on any medicines at the moment?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, a blood pressure tablet. Enalapril, twenty milligram, every morning. And aspirin, but that's on and off.
[SEG0030] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The aspirin from the chemist is a hundred milligrams. He's supposed to take it daily but he forgets half the time. The enalapril he does swallow.
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Maybe a hundred, I don't know, doctor. I take the aspirin when I remember, not every day. The enalapril I don't miss.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): How long have you had the high blood pressure?
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): Five-ish years, I suppose. I don't know the exact time. They started the tablet back then.
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any allergies to medicine?
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No allergies.
[SEG0036] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): What about penicillin? In your twenties you came out in a rash and the hospital said you were allergic. You've avoided it since.
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. I don't remember any rash. I don't think I'm allergic to anything.
[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): We'll leave that as not clear for now. Any heart trouble in the family?
[SEG0039] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): His brother had a stent put in, two years ago.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): It wasn't a stent. My brother had a bypass. That's the one thing I do know.
[SEG0041] person_3 (DOCTOR): Thanks. Do you smoke, or drink?
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): I stopped smoking about ten years ago. A brandy on a Friday, that's all. Oh, and the bakkie needs a new battery, but that's not your problem, hey.
[SEG0043] person_3 (DOCTOR): Let me have a listen. Chest is clear, heart sounds are normal, and there's no swelling of the ankles.

[SEG0044] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'm concerned this tight feeling when you exert yourself may be angina. I can't be certain yet. I'd like an ECG today and bloods, cholesterol, blood sugar, and kidney function.
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): Angina. I don't know, doctor. If you say so. Will it hurt, the ECG?

[SEG0046] person_3 (DOCTOR): The ECG is just stickers on the chest, it doesn't hurt. Carry on with the enalapril, twenty milligrams, every morning. If that tightness comes on and it doesn't settle when you rest, go straight to casualty. Come back in two weeks and we'll go through the results.

spec.situation: Man or woman 50-70 who comes 'for a check-up' and only slowly admits a tight feeling in the chest when climbing stairs or walking fast; first denies chest pain, later describes the tightness. Takes a BP tablet and aspirin on and off. Doctor orders ECG and bloods.
features: spoken_numbers: doses, vitals and durations are spoken as words or sloppy speech ('a hundred and two point five', 'one-forty over ninety', 'five-ish years', 'twenty milligram'); the label writes them normally (102.5, 140/90, 20 mg) and does not turn vague ones into exact ones.
relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.

bad.reason: Wife present and family says they moved into a flat in Morningside; living together is implied, not explicitly stated.
bad.text: living (description=Lives with his wife in a flat in Morningside, status=current, reported_by=family_member)

bad.reason: Sleep is not a neurological review detail in the transcript.

omissions.text: Patient explicitly denied chest pain ('No chest pain at all'); his symptom was chest tightness instead.
Chest tightness was described as 'across the chest'.
Family member stated the chest tightness occurs every time he takes the stairs, but the patient disputed this and said it is only when he rushes, not every time.
Doctor documented penicillin allergy status as unclear for now, rather than confirmed absence of allergies.
